subject.title: feat: raise (or remove) 3-minute no-output watchdog cap on CLI requests

question: Should ordinary inherited resumed CLI-backed runs keep the current 180-second no-output guard, get a higher core default, or rely on explicit per-backend watchdog configuration?
rationale: Current main intentionally preserves the 180-second guard for inherited user resumes while allowing cron and explicit/configured timeouts to lift it; changing that default affects both long silent work and runaway-process recovery.

options.title: Raise the inherited-resume default
options.body: Increase the default cap with focused resolver coverage while keeping existing per-backend overrides available for operators who need different behavior.

options.title: Document explicit per-backend tuning
options.body: Keep the current default and steer operators to `reliability.watchdog.resume` overrides for long-running silent CLI backends.

options.title: Adopt the broader config PR
options.body: Use the open broader PR as the vehicle, accepting that it also changes TUI streaming-watchdog configuration and needs separate proof.

recommendation.title: Raise the inherited-resume default
recommendation.body: Increase the default cap with focused resolver coverage while keeping existing per-backend overrides available for operators who need different behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: They merged the recent related resolver fix and are best positioned from the observed history to decide whether the preserved inherited-resume guard should change.
